posts.headline: Week 1 is officially here and One Nut Barner still hasn't uttered a single word — eight straight editions of silence from the owner of a 20-8 career record and 1.5 average finish, the most absurd résumé-to-hype gap in league history.
posts.detail: Zero rings despite the best regular-season pedigree in Busters Anonymous — if Put it in Ra doesn't show up loud in Week 1, this becomes the defining storyline of the year.

posts.headline: The excuses officially expired last edition and now Sasinci's World has to actually play a game — Big Head's title banner still sits on top of a losing 13-15 career record heading into Week 1.
posts.detail: A ring and a losing record don't add up, and Week 1 box scores are about to start settling the math for real.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh finally gets to play a real game, and the untalented tenth enters Week 1 still dragging the worst résumé in the league — a 4-10 record and dead-last 12th-place finish that no roster reshuffle has answered for.
posts.detail: This is the first chance in months for Chauncey to actually change the conversation instead of just absorbing it edition after edition.

posts.headline: Six-plus editions of total silence finally meet an actual football game — Thicks and the #FreeMaxx Champions open title defense with a 14-14 career record and 5.5 average finish that says the ring has been doing all the heavy lifting.
posts.detail: A reigning champ shouldn't need this many editions to say nothing; Week 1 is the first moment the results, not the banner, get to speak for Tyrique14.

posts.headline: The Clown Show rolls into Week 1 with the same middling 15-13 career mark and 4.0 average finish as always, and a fresh set of Week 1 lineups won't hide that this roster has topped out at respectable-but-forgettable for two straight years.
posts.detail: btkempski's best finish was a title back in year one, but a 7th-place worst finish since says the Alaskan Bull Worm act has been mostly bark — Week 1 is the chance to prove otherwise.
